title: Check yourself: moving code onto Java 11

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A pricing method declares `var discount = 0;` and then runs `discount += order.total() * 0.15;` once, for an order whose `total()` returns the double 30.0. It compiles with javac 21 and no -Xlint options. What does `discount` hold afterwards?

options.text: 4, since the variable is an int and += casts each result back to int
options.says: var takes int from the literal 0, and a compound assignment casts the double sum 4.5 back to int, dropping the fraction

options.text: 5, since the variable is an int and += rounds each result to the nearest int
options.says: the cast that += applies truncates toward zero; it does not round

options.text: 4.5, since var infers the type from every value the variable is assigned
options.says: var infers the type once, from the initializer; later assignments don't change it

options.text: 4.5, since var widens the variable to double when a double is first added
options.says: the type is fixed at the declaration, so the variable stays an int

origin.section: var Takes the Initializer's Type, Which Is Not Always the Type You Meant

questions.stem: A billing jar was compiled for Java 8. Its only use of `javax.xml.bind.DatatypeConverter` is inside the monthly statement export. The jar is deployed unchanged on Java 21, with no new dependencies. What happens?

options.text: It starts, and the first export throws NoClassDefFoundError, since a class is loaded when code first needs it
options.says: the JVM loads a class on first use, and java.xml.bind is not in the JDK after 11, so the error waits for the export

options.text: It starts, and the first export succeeds, since class files built for 8 keep the class library they were built against
options.says: old class files run against the running JDK's own class library, which no longer holds javax.xml.bind

options.text: It stops at startup with NoClassDefFoundError, since a jar's classes are loaded when the jar is opened
options.says: classes are loaded on first use, so the service starts and the error waits for the export

options.text: It stops at startup with UnsupportedClassVersionError, since class files built for 8 are refused by a newer JVM
options.says: newer JVMs run older class files; the page's Token class, built for 8, started on 21

origin.section: Java 11 Removed the Java EE Modules, and Code Built for 8 Fails at Its First Use

questions.stem: A service's class files were built for Java 8 and fail on Java 21 with a NoClassDefFoundError for `javax/xml/bind/DatatypeConverter`. Without rebuilding them, a developer puts `jakarta.xml.bind:jakarta.xml.bind-api:4.0.2` on the run-time class path. What does the next run of that code path do?

options.text: It still fails with NoClassDefFoundError, since the jar's classes are in a package with another name
options.says: the 4.x API jar holds jakarta.xml.bind.DatatypeConverter; javax.xml.bind is in the 2.3.x jars

options.text: It still fails with NoClassDefFoundError, since a package the JDK once had can't be loaded from the class path
options.says: the 2.3.3 jar on the class path fixes the same program on 21, so the class path is not refused

options.text: It runs, since the jar's classes are in the package the code imports
options.says: the package moved with Jakarta EE 9; the 4.0.2 jar has no javax.xml.bind classes

options.text: It runs, since the jar adds an alias for the package the code imports
options.says: nothing maps the names; the old class is simply not in the jar

origin.section: Java 11 Removed the Java EE Modules, and Code Built for 8 Fails at Its First Use

questions.stem: On Java 21, the directory `tools/` holds `Rotate.java`, which declares `public class Rotate` with a `main` method that calls `Paths2.archiveName(...)`, and `Paths2.java`, which declares `class Paths2`. Nothing has been compiled. Someone runs `java tools/Rotate.java app.log`. What happens?

options.text: Compilation fails at the call to Paths2, since the launcher compiles only the file named on the command line
options.says: Java 21's source launcher compiles one file in memory; other classes must be in it or compiled on the class path

options.text: Compilation fails at the class declaration, since a file run by the launcher may not declare a public class
options.says: a public class with main is the usual shape of a single-file program

options.text: The program runs, since the launcher compiles every .java file in the directory of the one named
options.says: Java 21 compiles only the named file; from Java 22 (JEP 458) the launcher also compiles other source files from the program's directory

options.text: The program runs, since the launcher compiles each source file that the named one refers to
options.says: Java 21 compiles only the named file; finding referenced source files came with JEP 458 in Java 22

origin.section: java Report.java Compiles One File in Memory and Runs Its First Class

concepts: Code compiled for Java 8 that uses javax.xml.bind starts on Java 11 and later and throws NoClassDefFoundError only when that code first runs.
The 2.3.x jakarta.xml.bind-api jar restores the javax.xml.bind package; the 4.x jar holds jakarta.xml.bind, so old code still fails with it.
Java 21's source launcher compiles only the file it is given; Java 22 and later also compile other source files from its directory.
var takes the type of its initializer once, so var total = 0 is an int that += silently truncates.
